question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>r</mi></math> be non-zero complex numbers and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> be the set of solutions <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>y</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℝ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfenced></math> of the equation <math><mi>s</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, where <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>-</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>y</mi></math>. Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?

options.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> has exactly one element, then <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>≠</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>

If <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> has infinitely many elements

The number of elements in <math><mi>L</mi><mo>∩</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{" separators="|"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>:</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>
If L has more than one element, then L has infinitely many elements

solution.text:
Given
sz+tz-+r=0 ...(i)
On taking conjugate s-z-+t-z+r-=0 ...(ii)
zs2-t2=r-t-rs-
1 If s≠t then z has unique value
2 If s=t then r-t-rs- may or may not be zero so L may be empty set
3 Locus of z is null set or singleton set or a line in all cases it will intersect given circle at most two points.
4 In this case locus of z is a line so L has infinite elements
